resources.string:
Version %2$s, %1$s
Start again to update to version %3$s
Start by connecting to a computer
Connect to a computer, enable USB debugging, and run this command. Run it again after restarting the device:\n\n%1$s
There are some other considerations, please confirm that you have read the help first.
Wireless debugging needs %1$s on this Android version.
Local network access is required for Wireless debugging.

Please enable "Wireless debugging" in "Developer options". "Wireless debugging" is automatically disabled when network changes.\n\nNote, do not disable "Developer options" or "USB debugging", or Shevery will be stopped.
Please try to disable and enable "Wireless debugging" if it keeps searching.
Port is an integer ranging from 1 to 65535.
Can\'t connect to wireless debugging service.
Wireless debugging is not enabled.\nNote, before Android 11, to enable wireless debugging, computer connection is a must.

Please start paring by the following steps: "Developer Options" - "Wireless debugging" - "Pairing device using pairing code".\n\nAfter the pairing process starts, you will able to input the pairing code.
The system requires the pairing dialog always visible, using split-screen mode is the only way to let this app and system dialog visible at the same time.
Unable to generate key for wireless debugging.\nThis may be because KeyStore mechanism of this device is broken.
Please go through the pairing step first.
A notification from Shevery will help you complete the pairing.
Enter "Developer options" - "Wireless debugging". Tap "Pair device with pairing code", you will see a six-digit code.
Enter the code in the notification to complete pairing.
The pairing process needs you to interact with a notification from Shevery. Please allow Shevery to post notifications.
MIUI users may need to switch notification style to "Android" from "Notification" - "Notification shade" in system settings.
Otherwise, you may not able to enter paring code from the notification.
Please note, left part of the "Wireless debugging" option is clickable, tapping it will open a new page. Only turing on the switch on the right is incorrect.
Back to Shevery and start Shevery.
Shevery needs to access local network. It is controlled by the network permission.

Some systems (such as MIUI) disallow apps to access the network when they are not visible, even if the app uses foreground service as standard. Please disable battery optimization features for Shevery on such systems.

In addition, Shevery can be started automatically on boot. If not, please check if your system or third-party tools have restricted Shevery.
You can refer to %s.
Apps that has requested or declared Shevery will show here.
You need to take an extra step

Your device manufacturer has restricted adb permissions and apps using Shevery will not work properly.

Usually, this limitation can be lifted by adjusting some options in "Developer options". Please read the help for details on how to do this.

You may need to restart Shevery for the operation to take effect.
The permission of adb is limited

It\'s highly possible that your device manufacturer limits the permission of adb.

There may be a solution for your system in this document.
Try checking the spelling or resetting filters.
Granted for this session only; switch off to make it permanent
This app declares no runtime permissions
Run commands through Shevery in terminal apps you like
First, Export files to any where you want. You will find two files, %1$s and %2$s.

If there are files with the same name in the selected folder, they will be deleted.\n\nThe export function uses SAF (Storage Access Framework). It\'s reported that MIUI breaks the functions of SAF. If you are using MIUI, you may have to extract the file from Shevery\'s apk or download from GitHub.
Then, use any text editor to open and edit %1$s.
For example, if you want to use Shevery in %1$s, you should replace %2$s with %3$s (%4$s is the package name of %1$s).
Finally, move the files to somewhere where your terminal app can access, you will be able to use %1$s to run commands through Shevery.
Some tips: grant execute permission to %1$s and add it to %2$s, you will able to use %1$s directly.

With %1$s, in any terminal app, you can connect to and interact with the shell runs by Shevery.

About the detailed usage %1$s, tap to view the document.
Use the pure black theme if night mode is enabled
Start on boot via Wireless debugging
On boot, briefly enable Wireless debugging and start Shevery over ADB (TCP port 5555). No root required, Wi-Fi is needed only for a moment.
On boot, briefly enable Wireless debugging and start Shevery over ADB. No root required, Wi-Fi is needed only for a moment.
TCP binding (port 5555) is off: wireless debugging will stay enabled.
Shevery is not running. Start the service first, then come back and enable this setting.
The automatic permission grant failed. Run this command from a computer to grant it manually:
How to use:\n1. Connect the device to a computer (USB or wireless debugging).\n2. In the terminal, run the command from the field above.
Sheverying is modified from the Shevery open source project.
You can start Shevery service now.
Allow the app to use Shevery.
Can\'t start service because root permission is not granted or this device is not rooted.

Legacy Shevery has been deprecated since March 2019. Also, legacy Shevery does not work on newer Android systems.

Please ask the developer of %1$s to update.

%1$s has modern Shevery support, but it\'s requesting legacy Shevery. This could because Shevery is not running, please check in Shevery app.

Legacy Shevery has been deprecated since March 2019.
Automation apps using the fixed built-in token will be able to start and stop the service. Enable connectors?
Restart ADB startup onto TCP port 5555 so Shevery can reconnect without relying on the changing Wireless Debugging port.
Shevery needs to restart to apply this TCP mode change.
Wi-Fi is required for the first restart because Shevery must connect to the current Wireless Debugging port before switching ADB to 5555.
Show a notification when the Shevery service stops unexpectedly (always shown while ErrorProtect(Watchdog) is on).
Show a notification when ErrorProtect(Watchdog) successfully restarts the service
Restart the Shevery service using the last launch method
Cannot start on boot: a required permission is not granted. Open Shevery and grant the permission first.
Waiting for device unlock to start…
Shevery could not start on boot. Open Shevery to check the issue.
Tap to open Shevery, or expand this notification to stop it.
Tap to open Shevery, or expand this notification to start it.
Writes the system setting so USB debugging stays enabled. This works after the service has granted secure-settings access. Turning this off stops re-enabling it.
After the service is running, hides the swipe lock so the next boot can start without unlocking. A PIN, pattern, or password is left unchanged. Turning this off brings the lock screen back.
When a pairing code is on screen, pair with it and use up that code. Turn this off first if a computer needs the code.
If the service is available, reboot this device.
Could not reboot. The service is not running, or the system refused.
Not running · last start was wireless debugging
Not running · last start was root
Lock off %1$s · auto-pair %2$s · crash restart %3$s · secure settings %4$s
The service is not running yet. The lock screen changes the next time it starts.
Could not change the lock screen. A password, or a vendor lock screen that ignores this switch, stays as it is.
Copy an action, package, or command and send it from an automation app.
Stop the running service. Day-to-day use does not need this.
Set up wireless debugging via accessibility
Confirm the wireless debugging prompt and fill in the pairing code automatically. Enable the Sheverying accessibility service once.
Confirms wireless debugging and reads the pairing code so Sheverying can start without extra taps.
Use a fixed bottom bar instead of the floating pill
Swipe left or right on the main screen to switch Home, Modules, Comput, Settings
Blur content while swiping between tabs and scrolling lists up or down
How fast blur ramps up with swipe speed: %1$d%%
Reactively monitor service health. Automatically restarts Shevery if issues or crashes are detected.
Restores the wireless debugging flag if the ROM cleared it (at ADB start and Wi-Fi reconnect). Never turns it off.
Pinned accessibility services will be restored if disabled

Shevery is running, but Persistent TCP Mode is currently disabled.\n\nEnabling TCP Mode allows Shevery to stay running and auto-reconnect in the background—even without Wi-Fi—until your device is restarted.

Broadcast control uses the same fixed built-in auth token on every installation (-e auth <token>). Enable connectors only for trusted automation apps. Existing configurations using the original default token remain compatible.
Authentication is required to use Shevery
Block permission popups and deny apps unless toggled in this list
Add the “auth” extra to your intent. You can find your token under Automation in Settings.
Make sure the token in your intent matches the one in Shevery Settings.
An automation intent was blocked because Shevery connectors are disabled in Settings. Tap to enable.
About shows the installed app version. Status shows the running service version. After updating the app, restart the service to use the new version.
